UnitStatement: BRIEF_SCHEMA defines the INIT-TASK dispatch contract for TASK + content-digest.
content-digest is used when EVALUATION needs one structured digest for one deliverable folder.
ScopePath should normally be the execution root for a content-digest run.
AllowedWriteTargets should be limited to the intended digest output path under _Evaluation/content-digests/.
The PURPOSE brief field states why a digest run exists.
The ScopePath brief field identifies the execution root.
The TaskSkill brief field must equal content-digest.
AllowedWriteTargets lists the digest output path for the run.
RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH identifies the target deliverable folder.
RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH identifies the digest output file.
ExpectedOutputs lists the expected single digest file.
content-digest defines no optional runtime overrides.
DELIVERABLE_PATH must identify exactly one deliverable folder.
OUTPUT_PATH must already have an existing parent directory under _Evaluation/content-digests/.
The content-digest run must remain single-deliverable and read-only on production files.
A valid content-digest run writes exactly one digest file to OUTPUT_PATH.
The digest must contain all seven required sections in the required order.
Identity fields must come from _CONTEXT.md or be explicitly marked absent.
Dependency counts and key upstream or downstream items must be derived only from deliverable-local files.
Quality observations must be specific factual flags rather than vague judgments.
A content-digest run must not modify any file in DELIVERABLE_PATH.
A content-digest run must not read any file outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest reports FAILED_INPUTS when DELIVERABLE_PATH is missing or is not a directory.
content-digest reports FAILED_INPUTS when the parent directory of OUTPUT_PATH does not exist.
Absent deliverable-local files do not fail the run by themselves and are reported as missing in the digest.
content-digest reads one deliverable folder and produces a structured seven-section content digest.
The content digest summarizes identity, scope, document kit, dependencies, references, semantic framework, and quality observations.
content-digest is a bounded semantic-matching extraction skill.
content-digest reads deliverable-local files and extracts structured information directly.
content-digest does not perform engineering judgment or cross-deliverable analysis.
Each content-digest invocation is dispatched by EVALUATION with a brief specifying the deliverable path and output location.
Each content-digest invocation produces one digest file.
content-digest uses the TASK generic shell mode with no profile.
The typical content-digest dispatcher is EVALUATION, batched by package with one dispatch per deliverable.
ScopePath is a required input and is set to the execution root.
AllowedWriteTargets is a required input for the execution-root _Evaluation/content-digests/ location.
RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH is a required absolute path to the deliverable folder.
RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH is a required absolute path to the digest output file.
DEL-ID is derived at runtime from _CONTEXT.md or inferred from the deliverable folder name.
DEL Name is derived at runtime from _CONTEXT.md.
PKG-ID is derived at runtime from _CONTEXT.md.
content-digest has no optional runtime overrides.
DELIVERABLE_PATH must be a valid directory path containing _CONTEXT.md.
OUTPUT_PATH must be under _Evaluation/content-digests/{PKG-ID}/ with an existing parent directory.
content-digest reads are limited to files within the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest reads _CONTEXT.md in full for identity, description, acceptance criteria, and scope traceability.
content-digest reads _DEPENDENCIES.md in full for tracking mode, upstream/downstream summary, and register statistics.
content-digest reads _REFERENCES.md in full for source document pointers.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Datasheet.md for key parameters and structured metadata.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Specification.md for requirements and scope definition.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Guidance.md for design rationale, principles, and considerations.
content-digest reads only the first 80 lines of Procedure.md for execution workflow.
content-digest reads only the first 40 lines of _SEMANTIC.md for framework type and perspective.
content-digest must not read outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest must not cross into adjacent deliverable folders or scan package-level or project-level registers.
content-digest writes are limited to exactly one file at RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH.
The parent directory of OUTPUT_PATH must already exist, and content-digest does not create it.
content-digest uses no deterministic tools.
content-digest is a reasoning-first, semantic-matching extraction skill.
content-digest intentionally omits the allowed-tools frontmatter field.
content-digest must not write outside OUTPUT_PATH.
content-digest must not modify any file in DELIVERABLE_PATH.
content-digest must not read files outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest must not perform cross-deliverable scanning or comparison.
The precondition step validates that DELIVERABLE_PATH exists and is a directory.
If DELIVERABLE_PATH is not a directory, content-digest reports RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS.
The precondition step validates that the parent directory of OUTPUT_PATH exists.
If OUTPUT_PATH has no existing parent directory, content-digest reports RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS.
content-digest reads each file listed in the read boundary while respecting its read scope.
If a read-boundary file is absent, content-digest records that fact and does not fail.
content-digest extracts package, discipline, type, and responsible identity fields from _CONTEXT.md.
content-digest extracts description, acceptance criteria, SOW traceability IDs, and objective traceability IDs from _CONTEXT.md.
content-digest extracts a one-sentence focus summary for Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure.
content-digest extracts tracking mode, upstream count, downstream count, key upstream, and key downstream from _DEPENDENCIES.md.
content-digest extracts the list of all referenced documents from _REFERENCES.md.
content-digest extracts whether _SEMANTIC.md is present and the framework type if identifiable.
content-digest scans read content for TBD items and their resolution authority.
content-digest scans read content for ASSUMPTION labels and their rationale.
content-digest scans read content for placeholder text or incomplete sections.
content-digest scans read content for Conflict Table entries with HumanRuling status.
content-digest scans read content for enrichment markers such as A-001 and B-001.
content-digest scans read content for inconsistencies between documents within the folder.
content-digest quality observations are factual flags, not evaluative judgments.
content-digest writes the structured digest to OUTPUT_PATH using the defined seven-section structure.
content-digest overwrites the digest file if it already exists.
The digest file contains exactly seven sections in order.
The digest Identity section includes package, discipline, type, and responsible fields.
The digest Scope section includes description, acceptance criteria, SOW traceability, and objective traceability.
The digest Document Kit Summary section includes Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure focus summaries.
The digest Dependencies section includes tracking mode, upstream count, downstream count, key upstream, and key downstream.
The digest References section lists all referenced documents.
The digest Semantic section states whether _SEMANTIC.md is present and gives the framework type if identifiable.
The digest Quality Observations section lists TBDs, placeholders, and inconsistencies with IDs where available.
Missing information is noted as not present or TBD in source.
The digest output must not leave placeholder braces in the file.
content-digest outputs one digest file at RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH containing the seven required sections.
content-digest is read-only on deliverable production documents.
content-digest processes exactly one deliverable folder per run.
content-digest reports what source files contain and does not infer, speculate, or fill gaps.
content-digest marks missing information explicitly.
content-digest uses semantic matching rather than deep reasoning.
content-digest flags quality observations without performing engineering judgment.
content-digest produces one digest per run.
content-digest preserves the seven-section structure in the specified order.
EVALUATION_REPORT, not content-digest, is responsible for evaluative assessment of deliverable correctness.
content-digest QA expects all seven sections to be present in the output digest.
content-digest QA expects identity fields to be populated from _CONTEXT.md without invention.
content-digest QA expects SOW and OBJ traceability IDs to be listed or explicitly marked absent.
content-digest QA expects dependency counts to be stated with key upstream and downstream items named.
content-digest QA expects quality observations to be specific items with IDs where available.
content-digest QA expects no files in DELIVERABLE_PATH to be written or modified.
content-digest QA expects the digest to be written to the specified OUTPUT_PATH.
content-digest QA expects no files outside the deliverable folder to be read.
EVALUATION synthesizes content-digest outputs across packages.
EVALUATION_REPORT applies evaluative reasoning when scoring dimensions.
content-digest does not perform scoring or cross-deliverable synthesis.
content-digest first reads the bounded deliverable-local files listed in the skill contract.
content-digest then uses direct reasoning to extract and summarize structured information into the seven-section digest.
TASK enforces no deterministic tools for content-digest.
No deterministic tools are operationally invoked by content-digest.
content-digest performs bounded extraction and summarization only.
content-digest identifies quality-observation signals from deliverable-local files without crossing into engineering judgment or cross-deliverable synthesis.
content-digest tool policy disallows writes outside OUTPUT_PATH.
content-digest tool policy disallows modification of files in DELIVERABLE_PATH.
content-digest tool policy disallows reading files outside the specified deliverable folder.
content-digest tool policy disallows cross-deliverable scanning or comparison.
content-digest may write exactly one file at RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH.
